coverage_note: Building permits issued by New Hanover County — the county's own permit register, which covers Wilmington, Carolina Beach, Wrightsville Beach, Kure Beach, Castle Hayne, and the unincorporated county (the register's own place codes, proven against its ZIP codes at audit). Totals here are the county register's totals, labeled as such.

dedupe_rule.definition: One published permit = one PERMIT_NUMBER in New Hanover County's Building Permits layer. The layer's grain is one row per permit: no collapsing applies or is needed.
dedupe_rule.measurement: Scoped trailing-12-month window (ISSUE_DATE >= 2025-11-20, ISSUE_DATE <= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, non-construction record types excluded — see pull_where_extra), measured 2026-11-20 against the live layer: 20,368 rows = 20,368 distinct PERMIT_NUMBER (and 20,368 distinct PMPERMITID and OBJECTID), 0 duplicates. The pipeline's in-batch duplicate gate and the (county_id, source_record_id) upsert key guard every future pull.

field_map.address: Assembled from the county's address parts (NUMBER + SUBNUM + DIR + STREET + TYPE, plus UNIT when the county states one), title-cased from the county's all-caps printing. Present on 20,117 of 20,368 scoped window permits; blank where the county publishes no street address, never inferred.
field_map.application_date: APPLICATION_DATE (epoch ms in the ArcGIS feed, converted to the civil date). Present on 100% of window permits.
field_map.category: From the county's own permit-type prefix: types naming Residential (14,248 scoped window permits) publish Residential, types naming Commercial (5,249) publish Commercial; the remaining types (land disturbance, stormwater, floodplain, well/septic and similar county permits, 871) carry no class and stay NULL, never inferred.
field_map.city: The county publishes a two-letter place code; at audit each code was proven against the ZIP codes on its own rows — WM = Wilmington (ZIPs 28401/28403/28405/28409/28411/28412), CB = Carolina Beach (28428), CH = Castle Hayne (28429), WB = Wrightsville Beach (28480), KB = Kure Beach (28449) — and is expanded to the place name on that evidence. Rows with no code (281 unscoped) stay NULL.
field_map.contractor_rule: GENERAL_CONTRACTOR ONLY — the county's published licensed general contractor of record, carried verbatim as the county prints it, state license annotation included (present on about a quarter of window permits; 75 sampled at audit — every one a licensed contractor or firm, zero OWNER/owner-builder tokens). PROJECT_CONTACT and ASSIGNED_TO are never requested: they name individuals (project contacts and county staff), not the contractor business of record.
field_map.issue_date: ISSUE_DATE (epoch ms, converted). The window is defined on it, bounded at both ends: the trailing 12 months ending at pull time (ISSUE_DATE <= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP in pull_where_extra). Exactly 2 permits in the whole layer carry junk future issue dates (the raw layer maximum is 2027-06-15); they fall outside the window's end by definition, are named here, and are the only window-adjacent records so excluded (measured 2026-11-20).
field_map.permit_number: PERMIT_NUMBER — verified exactly unique in the scoped window (20,368 distinct = 20,368 rows, 2026-11-20 audit).
field_map.permit_type_source: PERMIT_TYPE, the county's own permit family (Residential/Commercial Building, the named trade families, Trade Permit, Accessory, Addition, Demolition, Sign, Land Disturbance, Stormwater, Floodplain, OSWP well/septic, Building Safety Fire, and others), with WORK_CLASS carried in the pull for trade classification only.
field_map.project_description: DESCRIPTION, the county's own scope text (present on 98%+ of window permits).
field_map.scope_filter: pull_where_extra excludes record types that authorize no construction (994 of 21,362 bounded-window permits): the county Environmental Health FLI family — food, lodging and institution operating licenses and inspections (847: public swimming pool operating permits, body art, temporary food establishments, change-of-ownership, limited food, mobile units, display spas, remodels) — plus fire operational permits (118: tents and air-supported structures, foster care, daycare/group home, carnivals and fairs, fireworks, open flames, spraying or dipping, fuel dispensing, general use), the Zoning Permit (18), the Commercial Facility License (10), and the Residential Occupancy Certification (1). Kept deliberately: land-disturbance, stormwater and floodplain permits, OSWP well and septic permits, and Building Safety Fire permits (alarms, sprinklers, extinguishing systems) — families authorizing physical work on a site. Each excluded type is named and counted here and on the Data Sources page (the Alachua/San Antonio scope-filter treatment).
field_map.status: PERMIT_STATUS, mapped through status_map; the verbatim source value is kept in status_source. Scoped window statuses are post-issuance lifecycle states (Complete, Issued, certificates issued, Expired, and small residues) — every window record carries an issue date, so they stay in the population (the Raleigh treatment).
field_map.valuation: COUNTS-ONLY (the Austin/Seattle outcome, measured 2026-11-20): the layer's VALUATION field states the WHOLE PROJECT's value, restated identically on every sibling permit the project pulls. On the bounded window: 14,681 of 21,362 permits state $0, and values above $1M repeat on 499 excess sibling rows — one Wilmington hospital project's $65,184,998 appears on both its commercial mechanical and its commercial electrical permit, and one Center Point project's $58,189,381 appears four times — injecting $4,798,119,099 of restatement, 71% of the raw $6,726,518,167 sum. No project key exists in the layer to dedupe by (PROJECT is null on the sibling rows), so no trustworthy per-permit or aggregate dollar figure exists. The field is therefore NOT requested in pull_select at all: no dollar figure enters our data, none is published or aggregated, and none is estimated. The reason is stated openly on the hub, the Data Sources page, and in llms.txt.

history_range: 489,856 rows at audit (the county's register, 1976 to present in samples, including legacy rows); we backfill the trailing 12 months only (site rule).
license: New Hanover County ArcGIS open data (public access, county-published); attribution: New Hanover County, North Carolina
pull_where_extra: ISSUE_DATE <= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP AND PERMIT_TYPE NOT LIKE 'NHC FLI%' AND PERMIT_TYPE NOT IN ('NHC Zoning Permit','NHC Commercial Facility License','NHC Residential Occupancy Certification','NHC Fire Tent or Air Supported Structure','NHC Fire Foster Care','NHC Fire Fireworks/Pyrotechnics','NHC Fire Carnivals & Fairs','NHC Fire Spraying or Dipping','NHC Fire Open Flames and Candles','NHC Fire Daycare/Group Home','NHC Fire Fuel Dispensing','NHC Fire General Use')
rate_limit: ArcGIS FeatureServer query on the county's own GIS server, 1,000-row pages (the layer's maxRecordCount) with the adapter's 0.4s pacing plus retries; anonymous public tier served the full audit and backfill pulls steadily (count queries on this server are slow, ~40s, but paged pulls run ~5s/page).
source_name: New Hanover County open data — Building Permits (county GIS)
terms_status: verified-open-2026-11-20: the Building Permits layer is published by New Hanover County on the county's official GIS server (gis.nhcgov.com) with public access, alongside the county's other public thematic layers. Figures are published 'as reported by New Hanover County' with attribution; no endorsement is implied.
update_cadence: County register updated as permits issue (daily on business days); MEASURED 2026-11-20: freshest bounded ISSUE_DATE 2026-11-18 (two days before the audit pull) and scoped monthly volumes steady through October 2026. The layer publishes no editingInfo stamp, so freshness (gate 5) is measured as the freshest ISSUE_DATE at or before the pull moment (freshness_stamp_field + freshness_stamp_where) under a 168h threshold sized to a business-day issuer — the DeKalb/Philadelphia treatment, bounded against the layer's two junk future-dated legacy rows.
watermark_field: ISSUE_DATE + PERMIT_NUMBER — refresh re-pulls by the ISSUE_DATE watermark (same window predicate, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP end bound and scope filter) and upserts.
